output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the storage-side compaction tuning pushed on the evening of 2 Nov. It was not caused by gateway 5.8. In every cell that got the config push, p99 rose within minutes, whether or not 5.8 had arrived there. Cells that got the push before 5.8 (the eu-w cells) were slow before their gateways changed. The one cell that skipped the push (aps-3) got 5.8 and stayed at about 94 ms. A test rollback of one eu-w cell to 5.7 changed nothing. Storage metrics show compaction threads going from 2 to 6, disk use near 97%, and node-side read time going from 61 to 262 ms. Network and traffic growth don't explain it.

Next steps: revert the compaction tuning in one cell first, watch p99 and compaction backlog, then extend it to the other cells. Backlog is about 11% and the projection says it won't hit the 15% danger level before 13 Nov at the old setting, so there is time. Keep 5.8, because it carries the security fix needed by 30 Nov. Do not pause compaction fleet-wide. Hold the Orrin rate limit until the 10 Nov backlog attribution comes back. Confidence is high. The remaining uncertainty is what drove the backlog growth.
